1375: Near Bloomingdale and Rockville (Parke County), with a fishing pond; also primitive sites and cabins. --Claude
1383: Family campground on the Tippecanoe River at Monterey, with a pool, a sandy river beach, playgrounds, an outdoor movie screen and live music on holiday weekends; it runs canoe, kayak and tube trips on the river.  The tent and primitive sites are on the riverbank; the 90-plus RV sites sit back from it, with a river view at best. --Claude
1387: Gravel-pad sites 2 miles west of Turkey Run State Park, with a canoe livery on Sugar Creek; the sites are wooded and set back from the creek. --Claude
1480: Stetson's Tumble Hill campground at Cohocton. --Claude
1489: At Davenport in the Catskill foothills, on a 15-acre spring-fed lake that some sites overlook; seasonal campers share the park with overnight ones. --Claude
1509: Half a mile from the Darien Lake theme park's main entrance at Darien Center, with a view of the park and its nightly fireworks; Darien Lake admits only vehicles, so concertgoers drive or take a taxi.  The sites are shaded and spacious, mainly for tents; RVs dry camp, and only quiet inverter generators are allowed. --Claude
1510: At Diamond Point near Lake George, with about a mile of Schroon River frontage, a pool, a beach and kayaks.  Open mid-May to mid-October. --Claude
1512: Off I-87 Exit 39 at Plattsburgh, with more than 200 big-rig sites, many of them seasonal, and a heated pool; the Lake Champlain beach is a walk away, though no site is on the water. --Claude
1518: On the Schroon River between Brant and Loon Lakes near Chestertown, minutes from Lake George, with a pool, a game room, and a launch for canoes and tubes; tubes, canoes and rowboats are for rent.  Open from late May to early October (May 20 to October 9 in 2023, the latest season the operator posts). --Claude
1570: Corps of Engineers campground on Rough River Lake at Falls of Rough, run for the 2026 season by the concessionaire BrightSky Campgrounds.  36 of the sites have water and electric.  The RV sites are tiered down the hillside and overlook the cove, though most are not on the water; the hilltop basic sites are away from the lake.  Boat ramp, fishing pier, disc golf and a playground. --Claude
1571: Corps of Engineers campground on Rough River Lake at McDaniels, run for the 2026 season by the concessionaire BrightSky Campgrounds.  50 of the sites have electric; several are on the water and the rest a short walk from it.  Beach, boat ramp, fishing pier, two group shelters and a playground. --Claude
1572: Corps of Engineers shoreline campground on Green River Lake near Campbellsville, run for the 2026 season by the concessionaire BrightSky Campgrounds.  20 of the sites have water and electric, and several are on the water.  Boat ramp, courtesy docks, fishing pier, swimming beach, playground and a hiking trail. --Claude
1732: Family RV park at West York with two ponds, a swimming pool, mini golf, a playground and trails; also tent sites and cabins. --Claude
1741: 35-acre resort at Topeka with a pool, mini golf, fishing ponds and planned activities.  Many sites are seasonal, but nightly sites are sold to anyone, with no membership. --Claude
1748: About 148 acres near Vienna on a 25-acre private lake, bordering the Shawnee National Forest, with more than 200 sites, cabins, a clubhouse and fishing.  Popular with horse riders but not limited to them; big rigs fit. --Claude
1760: Former KOA at Quincy on the Great River Road, with mostly concrete pads, a pool and a playground.  It overlooks the Mississippi: the river is across Bonansinga Drive, and some sites have a distant view of it. --Claude
1821: Monmouth County park in Freehold Township with a modern bathhouse.  Weekend stays need at least 2 nights. --Claude
1983: Family-owned park off I-35 Exit 106 near Eagleville, with gravel sites; 12 have full hookups and 9 are pull-throughs. --Claude
2606: RV-only park near historic downtown Florence, winterized for year-round stays; it sells nights, weeks and months, so some residents stay long-term. --Claude
2667: Run by Denver Water, the city's water utility.  The designated sites ring the reservoir, most of them RV-length (30 to 50 ft), each with a fire ring and picnic table; there is a boat launch.  At the East Campground many RV sites sit on the open, treeless shoreline, though not all are on the water.  Open about April 1 to November 30. --Claude
2766: Platte County Agricultural Society fairgrounds at Columbus, with 40 to 50 full-hookup sites among about 85 (the rest dry) and horse stalls.  Reviewers mention frequent passing trains and a somewhat run-down feel. --Claude
2782: Buffalo County park, the former Ravenna Lake State Recreation Area, turned over to the county about 20 years ago, so no Nebraska park permit is needed.  8 primitive sites, 9 electric-only, 16 with water and electric and 8 premium pull-throughs with water and electric; the bathhouse opened in spring 2022.  Walk-up sites are paid at the iron ranger by the entrance and can fill quickly. --Claude
2830: City of Gering RV park at the foot of Scotts Bluff National Monument, with concrete pads and a view of the monument.  Monthly stays are sold only from November 1 to March 31; the dump station is closed November 1 to May 1. --Claude
